prompt: A line passes through the points $(2, 7)$ and $(6, 19)$. What is the slope of the line?
hint: Slope compares two changes between the points. Which change goes on top and which goes on the bottom?

hints.text: Slope compares two changes between the points. Which change goes on top and which goes on the bottom?
The rise is the change in $y$, which is $19 - 7$. The run is the change in $x$, which is $6 - 2$. Divide the rise by the run.
The rise is $12$ and the run is $4$, so the slope of the line is $\dfrac{12}{4} = 3$.

learningObjective: Compute the slope of a line through two given points.
explanation: Slope is the change in $y$ divided by the change in $x$, so write $\dfrac{19 - 7}{6 - 2}$ using the two points in the same order.
Simplify the top and bottom separately to get $\dfrac{12}{4}$, which equals $3$.
Reversing the order of the points gives $\dfrac{-12}{-4}$, which is also $3$, so the slope of the line is $3$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Where the sign errors come from
steps: The one dangerous mistake is subtracting the $y$ values in one order and the $x$ values in the other.
$\dfrac{19 - 7}{2 - 6} = \dfrac{12}{-4} = -3$ — right magnitude, wrong sign, and it will be one of the answer choices.
Write both differences top-to-bottom in the same order every time and this error disappears.
